September 29, 2026
A new Pro plan with Astra Ultrafast

We’re introducing Pro 500, a new $500/month plan with the highest included usage of the Pro plans and access to Astra Ultrafast in ChatGPT Work and Codex. Select Ultrafast in the model picker to use a faster service tier for GPT-6 Astra. It uses your included allowance first, then your credit balance after that allowance is used.
Among Pro plans, Ultrafast is available only with Pro 500. Buying credits on Pro 100 or Pro 200 does not unlock it. Pro 500 subscriptions are available through ChatGPT on the web at launch.
Learn more about ChatGPT Pro tiers.
Codex Cloud

Codex Cloud lets you start and continue coding tasks from desktop, web, or mobile using reusable environments with your project’s repositories, tools, and dependencies. Each task gets its own isolated workspace, and tasks can continue while your computer is asleep. In managed workspaces, your workspace’s Codex cloud-access settings apply.
To connect repositories and prepare an environment, see: Set up and configure Codex Cloud. For availability and usage, see: Using Codex with your ChatGPT plan.
Create and collaborate on Pages

Turn a conversation into a Page, start from a template, or begin writing directly in Space. Edit the text yourself or ask ChatGPT to revise it, add charts, or create interactive content. Collaborators can work on the same Page and leave comments, with each person using their own ChatGPT.

Pages follow Space’s availability and sharing settings. Sharing a Page does not give other people access to your private chats or memory; information added to the Page is visible to people who can view it.
Creating, editing, and scheduling Sites
Site owners and editors on Plus and Pro can select Edit site from a published Site in a desktop browser to continue editing in ChatGPT, review changes, and publish when ready.
Site owners can also create recurring cloud schedules from Automations. These updates are available where Sites is supported. Learn more about creating and managing Sites.
GPT-6.1 Sol in ChatGPT Work and Codex

GPT-6.1 Sol improves on GPT-6 Sol in agentic coding, computer use, and professional work. We’re rolling it out in ChatGPT Work and Codex, starting with Pro users and expanding to Plus, Business, Enterprise, and Edu. Enterprise and Edu workspace owners can enable model access in Workspace settings > Permissions & roles, on the Workspace tab or through a custom role. Learn how to manage model access with role-based access control.
For availability and model selection, see: ChatGPT Work and Codex.
Meet your dot

We’re introducing dots: always-on agents in ChatGPT that can take on ongoing work and keep making progress between conversations. Give your dot a goal, connect the apps it needs, and define what it can do on its own. Powered by GPT-6 Astra, your dot has its own cloud computer and can bring results back for your review.

Dots are rolling out gradually to eligible Pro and Business Premium users aged 18 and older in supported markets. Pro access excludes the European Economic Area, Switzerland, and the UK at launch. Enterprise access is a beta and is off by default. Create your dot in the ChatGPT desktop app or on desktop web.
For the next month, dots usage won’t count toward eligible Pro, Business, and Enterprise users’ plan allowances. After this period, we’ll share usage terms for each plan.
Learn more about getting started with your dot.
Meetings plugin

Available to eligible Pro, Business, and Enterprise users in the ChatGPT desktop app and on the web. Sharing in managed workspaces follows your organization’s settings; Enterprise sharing is an opt-in preview.

Learn more about Sign in with ChatGPT.

More controls in temporary chat

We’re rolling out new controls in temporary chat. You can now choose to personalize responses in a temporary chat with memory, plugins, and custom instructions from your regular chat settings. You can also choose to save a temporary chat.
How it works

Personalized: When you create a temporary chat, you can choose to have personalized responses. Personalized temporary chats can use your memories, custom instructions, and plugins to tailor responses. They do not create new memories and remain out of your chat history unless you save them. Personalization can be set only when you start a temporary chat and cannot be changed after the conversation begins.
Non-personalized: By default, temporary chats are not personalized. Non-personalized temporary chats do not use memory, custom instructions, or plugins, and they do not create new memories.

Saving a temporary chat: When a conversation becomes useful for the future, you can add it to your chat history. Saving converts it into a regular chat, so it then follows your account-level personalization settings and model-improvement preferences. For example, if you have memory enabled and save a temporary chat, this will become part of your chat history and can be referenced to personalized future responses.

ChatGPT Work can now complete tasks on signed-in websites
ChatGPT Work’s browser on web and mobile can also help you get tasks done on some websites that require you to sign in—so you can hand off a task and step away while it keeps working.

To get started, just ask ChatGPT Work to complete your task. If a website allows authentication, ChatGPT will surface the login screen so you can securely enter your credentials. You may also need to enter a security code. Once you’re signed in, ChatGPT can continue working. Your session may remain signed in for future tasks, so you don’t have to log in again every time. ChatGPT Work’s browser supports the use of password managers for simple, safe login. ChatGPT cannot see your username or password, and they are never seen by the model or used in model training. ChatGPT does not store your username or passwords. You can delete your browsing history from all sites or one site individually at any time from Settings > Cloud browser > Browser data.

Updated API errors so applications can distinguish traffic that increases too quickly from temporary model overload.

Let skills in Gemini tackle your most repetitive tasks

What: Today we’re rolling out skills directly into the Gemini chat globally1. Skills are a reusable set of instructions that tell Gemini how to handle specific tasks. Think of them as saved shortcuts to faster prompting.

Gemini can now help you build custom skills from your chats and automatically run them whenever you enter a matching prompt. For bigger tasks, you can stack multiple skills together at the same time — like combining a writing style skill with a brand guidelines skill to create on-brand assets in your voice.

Skills will soon replace Gems as the tool for tailoring instructions for specific tasks. To make this transition seamless, we will automatically migrate your Gems into skills when Gems go away. You can learn more about how to transition your Gems into skills by visiting our help center.

Why: We want to help you spend less time prompting and more time doing. With skills, you can save your most-used instructions once and run them endlessly – so you can skip the repetitive prompting and jump straight to the results.
